prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Repaint this existing full-bleed portrait game ability illustration in a MUCH looser, softer watercolor manner. Preserve the exact character identity, species, color marking locations, expression, depicted action, pose, camera framing, prop placement and composition. Keep the same portrait 63:88 artwork with no lettering or frame.
Make a decisive brushwork change: a small number of BIG WATER-DILUTED WET-ON-WET WASHES and broad soft brush dabs. Merge fur into large cloudy masses. Feather pigment boundaries, diffuse uneven edges, controlled color bleed and lost-and-found contours. Erase fine fur clumps, triangular serrations, veins, little flecks, dense foliage details and repeated tiny brush marks. NO embossed/gritty/granular texture or paper-noise filter. It should look swiftly hand-painted with a large wet brush on smooth paper, not a highly detailed illustration with a watercolor texture.
Use noticeably softer colors: diluted warm ochre/apricot/copper, creamy ivory, smoky blue/slate gray, dusty lavender/mauve for slime, muted sage/olive and softened blue-gray woodland washes. Lift the heavy near-black/navy background and reduce harsh orange-purple saturation, retaining enough charcoal identity contrast to recognize the tricolor dog or tortoiseshell cat. Background dissolves into a few atmospheric color pools, no crisp leaf clusters or sparkling dots. Keep only a few rich pigment accents. No uniformly sharp perimeter. A few sparse broken ink accents at eyes, nose, mouth and important contact points only. Keep the face and specific action readable at card scale, not blurry. Preserve all anatomy and paw count. No flame tail on the dog; no new objects, text, border, watermark or signature. Upper title and lower description areas should stay quiet. Opaque full-bleed painting.
